top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a specific, separable invention (Katori's magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, Ye's strontium realisation at 10^-18) that is independently reproduced at RIKEN, JILA, NIST, PTB and SYRTE. The two names map onto concept and record realisation without an arbitrary cut. The overlap with the 1989, 2005 and 2012 prizes is manageable by wording the citation around the lattice clock and not the comb. P002 is a clean prediction-to-experiment line but the field is eight years old, the pairing mechanism is open and Cao is outside the three names, so I rank it second, above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for the laureates of P001 or P002; my Chalmers and circuit-QED background bears on a shortlisted but unslated candidate (B003), not on the slate
